The following lists of Biology Dissertation Title Examples may help inspire you and plan your biological research. The titles are grouped by https://cromwellwilkes.co.uk/ biological subfields for inspiration and motivation purposes:

Development of Novel Antibiotic Combinations to Overcome Multidrug Resistance

Focus: Identify synergistic combinations of drugs that inhibit bacterial survival through differing mechanisms of actions

Disciplines: Microbiology, Medicinal Chemistry, Pharmacology

Why? Monotherapies fail due to antibiotic resistance so combinations may inhibit pathways to resistance.

Targeting Mechanisms of Bacterial Resistance using CRISPR-Cas9 Based Gene Editing

Focus: Investigate whether gene editing technologies can disable antibiotic resistance genes in bacterial genomes.

Disciplines: Molecular Biology, Genomics

Why? Directly interfering with bacterial resistance genes is on the cutting edge of precision antimicrobial strategies.

AI Prediction of Antibiotic Resistance Mutations Associated With Pathogenic Bacteria

Focus: Utilization of machine learning to predict the resistance mutations in bacteria using genomic data sets.

Disciplines: Computational Biology, AI, Bioinformatics

Why? Predicting resistance versions will define new therapeutic targets before they emerge.

Assessment of Global AMR Surveillance Systems in Low-Resource Settings

Focus: Identify data gaps or limitations in WHO GLASS or national AMR surveillance programs

Disciplines: Global Health, Public Policy, Epidemiology

Why? Surveillance discrepancy limits the ability to effectively monitor AMR globally.

Behavioural Determinants of Antibiotic Misuse in Community and Hospital Settings: A Mixed-Methods Study

Focus: Identify why misuse persists even with public health messaging.

Disciplines: Public Health, Sociology, Medical Anthropology

Why? Behaviour change is at the crux of AMR containment; however behaviour change is understudied in this context.

Investigation Of Antimicrobial Peptides (Amps) As An Alternative To Conventional Antibiotics

Focus: Assess efficacy and toxicity of AMPs against resistant strains.

Disciplines: Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Pharmaceutical Sciences.

Reason for doing this: AMPs utilize non-traditional mechanisms for killing resistant bacterial.

Economic Evaluation of Antibiotic Stewardship Programs in Tertiary Care Hospitals

Focus: Evaluating the financial and clinical outcomes of stewardship interventions.

Disciplines: Health economics, hospital management.

Reason: Finance ministers/directors want to see a financial justification for implementing multi-year programs.

Discovery of Antimicrobial Agents from Medicinal Plants and Natural Sources.

Focus: Screen selected phytochemicals for antibacterial activity against MDR strains.

Disciplines: Pharmacognosy, ethnobotany.

Reason: Natural compounds have an underdeveloped drug discovery pipeline.

Consideration of Environmental Reservoirs of AMR in the Spread of AMR Genes.

Focus: Screen selected phytochemicals for antibacterial activity against MDR strains.

Disciplines: Environmental Microbiology, One Health.

Reason: AMR is not only a clinical issue—there are large environmental reservoirs that also contribute.

Incorporation of AMR into National Sustainable Development Goals: Policy and Governance Concerns.

Focus: Analyse how the AMR policy is represented (or missing) in national SDG documents.

Disciplines: International relations, public policy, global governance.

Reason: Multisectoral action is required to address AMR and the health ministry is not the only sector that needs to prioritize AMR.

Optional Add-ons for These Topics:

  • Align with WHO’s Global Action Plan on AMR
  • Align with UN SDG 3 (Health), SDG 6 (Water & Sanitation), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption), and SDG 17 (Partnerships)
  • Follow a One Health, FAO, OIE and UNEP framework
